purpose.summary: This subprogram saves a medical image for the ORCA (JMA standard receipt software) system. It base64-encodes an image file from a temporary directory, reads the encoded data, then inserts or updates a record in the 'tbl_med_image' database table via the MONFUNC database interface. After processing, it deletes the temporary file.
purpose.domain: healthcare / medical records (Japanese medical association receipt software)

notable_features: CALL 'system' to invoke shell commands (base64 encoding and rm -f) from COBOL
CALL 'MONFUNC' for database operations (DBSELECT, DBFETCH, DBINSERT, DBUPDATE, DBCLOSECURSOR) — ORCA-specific DB middleware
COPY of .INC and named copybooks (CPMEDIMAGE.INC, MCPAREA, MCPDATA.INC, CPORCSMIAREA.INC, COMMON-SPA)
Large PIC X(500000) image record and PIC X(510000) MCPREC field
Japanese comments encoded in EUC-JP (decoded as latin-1 artifacts)
LINKAGE SECTION with two parameters: ORCSMIAREA and SPA-AREA
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS — database access abstracted through MONFUNC calls
verdict.notes: The source file contains Japanese EUC-JP encoded comments that appear garbled because the file was decoded as latin-1. The program is clearly part of the open-source ORCA JMA medical receipt system (Japan Medical Association). The dialect is most likely GnuCOBOL given the CALL 'system' pattern and .INC copybook conventions used throughout the ORCA project.
